en: Mayon Volcano in Albay features a nearly perfect conical shape formed by layers of solidified lava and ash from its frequent historical eruptions.
The Philippine eagle is a critically endangered bird of prey endemic to the old-growth forests of the island of Mindanao.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley before emptying into the Babuyan Channel.
Lake Lanao in Mindanao is the second-largest lake in the Philippines and serves as a major source of hydroelectric power for the region.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly through a cave into the West Philippine Sea.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a protected marine sanctuary known for its pristine coral reefs and diverse marine life.
Baguio City in the Cordillera Administrative Region experiences a subtropical highland climate, making its average temperature significantly cooler than the rest of the Philippines.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
Taal Volcano in Batangas features a main crater lake situated on Volcano Island, which is entirely surrounded by the larger Taal Lake.
The tamaraw is a small, dwarf buffalo endemic to the island of Mindoro and is currently one of the most endangered bovines globally.
The Sierra Madre mountain range runs along the eastern coast of Luzon, acting as a natural barrier that shields the island from Pacific typhoons.
